latest.prompt:
PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere (letters, numbers, signage, labels, logos, watermarks, inscriptions).
2) One single scene filling the whole frame: no split panels, collage, frame, border, canvas-on-wall, poster, mockup, visible paper, matting or blank studio backdrop.
3) The image is the scene itself, never a photographed painting, print, mural or gallery piece.
4) Nothing from outside the moment's era: no later technology, clothing, materials or buildings.
5) No distorted anatomy (extra limbs or fingers, malformed hands or feet, warped faces).
6) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
7) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
8) Depict only the SELECTED CHARACTERS, including groups and no-form subjects. The shared look, source narrators and neighbors do not add cast; apply shared clothing only to selected characters.
If instructions conflict, follow them in this order: these rules, then the work brief, then the art style's rendering, then the section look, then the scene plan.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Exodus 16:15: "When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they didn’t know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread which Yahweh has given you to eat."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; The Israelite people (the children of Israel); God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel

FORMLESS SUBJECTS (binding depiction constraints, including when the source uses bodily metaphors):
- God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel: represent only through the non-figurative presence allowed by its canon and the work brief. No head, face, torso, limbs, hands, human silhouette or garment-shaped body, even faceless or made of light. Do not represent this subject as a figure occupying a seat.
These constraints apply only to the named subjects; other characters retain their own canon forms.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.
- the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.
- The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.
- Only Moses, The Israelite people (the children of Israel), the camp of Israel, The wilderness (Exodus route) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SECTION LOOK (shared by every image of this story section; the style's rendering outranks it):
Place: Open wilderness camp of Israel: scattered tents and the ground around them, pale dust and sand, a dewy plain beyond with the wilderness edge in view.
Time of day: Early morning as dew lifts into full daylight across the section.

SCENE PLAN (supporting; never overrides the rules, the brief, the style or the look):
Primary subject: Moses stands forward among the gathered people, turning toward them with a raised open hand; the people lean in, pointing at the small round flakes on the sand.
Action: Israelites crouch and touch the pale scattered flakes on the ground, murmuring to one another; Moses speaks, gesturing to the sky; radiance glows softly within the dense cloud above the camp.
Setting: Open wilderness camp: scattered tents, pale dust and sand, dew lifting from the ground, a dewy plain beyond with the wilderness edge in view.
Secondary elements: Wooden gathering baskets and jars on the ground; woven tunics, cloaks and linen head-cloths on the people; a dense slowly moving cloud resting over the camp with brilliant white-gold radiance veiled within it.
Mood: Wonder and puzzlement tempered by reverence; a quiet, grounded awe as the people discover an unfamiliar provision.
Time of day: Early morning as dew lifts into full daylight; cool clear desert air with soft dawn light on the sand.
Composition: Wide view from ground level among the people, Moses centred in the middle distance, the cloud and its glowing heart arching above, the camp and wilderness edge receding behind.

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).
